newsitem.title: THAILAND: Toyota to boost car exports from Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Toyota to boost car exports from Thailand.

text.p: Japan's Toyota Motor Corp said on Friday it planned to boost car exports from its Thai plants following completion and expansion of a second Thai car-assembly facility.

"We expect to increase our car exports assembled from Thai plants. The new advanced factories will raise our competitiveness in terms of pricing and quality," Toyota President Hiroshi Okuda told a news conference.
He was in Thailand to officially open Toyota's second eight billion baht ($307.7 million) plant located 80 km (50 miles) east of Bangkok.
The plant, completed last December, has initial production capacity of 50,000 vehicles a year but will expand capacity to 100,000 by the end of this year, Toyota said.
Toyota's first assembly plant is located in Samut Prakarn province, a suburb of Bangkok.
After the expansion, Toyota's total car production from its two plants would rise to 240,000 vehicles a year from 190,000 last year, Okuda said.

"The new plant will help boost our car exports into the region. We aim to export about 20,000 units or 10 percent of our total car production by the year 2000," said Yoshiaki Muramatsu, president of Toyota Motor (Thailand) Corp.
He did not give the number of how many cars were currently being exported from Toyota's Thai plants.
Toyota exports its latest compact passenger car, the Soluna, to Singapore and Brunei and its pick-up, the Hi-Lux, to 20 countries from its Thai assembly plants.
Okuda said Toyota's overseas production capacity outside Japan would reach two million vehicles next year from an expected total production of 1.45 million in 1997.
Of Toyota's 1998 overseas production, 1.2 million will be in North America, while 600,000 and 200,000 vehicles will be assembled in Asia and Europe respectively, he said.
Toyota officials said they expect car sales in Thailand this year to rise to 180,000 vehicles from 163,940 units in 1996.
"We expect to have a market share of over 30 percent this year or 180,000 units sold" said Muramatsu.
Toyota was Thailand's top car seller last year with 27.8 percent of the market.
Toyota car sales in 1997 will be supported by expected demand for its Soluna launched in late January, officials said.
"We estimate that about 50,000 units of Soluna models will be sold each year," Muramatsu said.
